sources.title: WebKit Features for Safari 27.0
sources.locator: Release heading/date; Media section; Updating to Safari 27; resolved issues
sources.observed_operation: Opened release article; inspected release date, desktop OS availability, media summary, and media-related resolved issues.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Safari 27.0 is available on macOS 26 and macOS 15; article does not announce a MediaRecorder MIME change, while the resolved-issues list includes microphone/session and MediaStreamTrack changes.
sources.applicability: Current desktop Safari version anchor; does not establish exact MediaRecorder format support.

sources.title: New WebKit Features in Safari 14.1
sources.observed_operation: Opened official WebKit release article and checked the MediaRecorder announcement.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Article says WebKit added MediaStream Recording/MediaRecorder support; it does not give a complete MIME support matrix.

sources.title: MediaStream Recording
sources.locator: §§2.1-2.3 and §6.1; constructor, start/stop, timeslice, completed chunk combination, resource exhaustion
sources.observed_operation: Opened fixed dated report and inspected surrounding constructor/start/stop/timeslice context and current published-version link.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A supported MIME probe is not proof that resources permit encoding; stop queues final dataavailable before stop; timeslice has a UA minimum; separate chunks need not be playable while completed combination must be.

sources.title: WebKit Features in Safari 18.4
sources.observed_operation: Opened official release article and inspected WebM/Opus, ALAC/PCM, and Ogg text with platform qualifiers.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Ogg Opus/Vorbis is qualified to macOS Sequoia 15.4, iOS/iPadOS 18.4, and visionOS 2.4; article does not supply a complete audio-only MIME matrix.
sources.applicability: Historical candidate evidence; not proof of Safari 27 runtime support.

sources.title: extendable-media-recorder issue 692
sources.released_version_or_commit: Opened 2025-08-08; reporter closed original report as completed 2025-08-12; later 2026 follow-up visible
sources.locator: Maintainer response, reporter AudioContext/MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode explanation and closure; later April 2026 follow-up
sources.observed_operation: Opened current issue history and inspected initial diagnosis, reporter follow-up/closure, and later similar report.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The original report concerned this library's Web Audio/channel-count path; maintainer pointed to two-channel track settings and reporter described a destination-node channel-count path. A later similar symptom remains a separate report.
sources.applicability: Library-specific test risk; does not establish a native Chrome/Safari defect or universal fix.

sources.title: High Resolution Time
sources.observed_operation: Opened fixed dated report and inspected monotonic clock and background timer exception.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A monotonic clock is not made inaccurate by background timer throttling, but timer callbacks may be throttled or frozen.
sources.applicability: Timekeeping basis only; does not guarantee scheduled stop execution.

sources.title: HTML Standard — Page visibility
sources.observed_operation: Opened current section and inspected visibility event task order.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Visibility update and visibilitychange firing are task-queued after the user agent determines a state change.
sources.applicability: Supports hidden-stop policy as a signal, not a hard real-time boundary.

findings.summary: Safari 26.0 is named current despite Safari 27.0 release on 2026-09-17; validation target is stale.
Five-minute meaning and over-limit outcome remain undecided; timer and visibility signaling cannot guarantee a hard boundary.
Released Safari Ogg Opus/Vorbis path is recorded in S05 but absent from candidate probes; either test with exact MIME evidence or intentionally exclude.
Safari 14.1 announcement is supported but lacks a source-map binding; C02 supplies it.
Current issue history includes channel-count diagnosis and reporter closure, omitted from the source note; library-specific caution remains appropriate.
